newsitem.title: USA: Buser starts final run for Iditarod victory.
newsitem.headline: Buser starts final run for Iditarod victory.

text.p: Martin Buser began the final 77-mile run Tuesday for the Nome finish line and a third championship in the Iditarod Trail Sled Dog Race.
Buser, who also won the world's most famous sled-dog race in 1992 and 1994, departed the Inupiat Eskimo village of White Mountain at 10:12 a.m. after completing a mandatory eight-hour layover there.
He was about 90 minutes ahead of his closest competitor, Doug Swingley, who was driving a slower and less-rested dog team.
The Swiss-born Buser, of Big Lake, Alaska, was expected in Nome early Tuesday evening.
Also in White Mountain Tuesday morning were two-time champion Jeff King and perennial contender DeeDee Jonrowe. They were expected into Nome, in third and fourth places, early Wednesday morning.
The 1,161-mile Iditarod began March 1 in Anchorage. Of the 53 mushers who began the race, eight had dropped out as of Tuesday.
